abstract: We separate the established low-energy quantum-gravity tier of Modal Triplet Theory (MTT) from its ultraviolet-completion problem. On a declared globally hyperbolic coherent background, the selected two-derivative Einstein–TEGR action admits the standard perturbative BV/BRST effective-field-theory construction, with gauge-invariant observables and the usual infrared graviton sector. We then re-examine the spectral proper-time (SPT) proposal. An exact graph theorem shows that Gaussian-damped lines control all loop directions if and only if their loop-momentum matrix has full rank; the mere presence of one damped graviton line is insufficient. We also prove that a nonzero propagator cannot simultaneously have a positive Källén–Lehmann/Stieltjes representation and permanent Gaussian decay in the same Euclidean spectral variable. Thus the earlier Stieltjes proof of unitarity for the Gaussian propagator is withdrawn, and SPT is retained only as a conditional filter/regulator model. The selected ultraviolet candidate is instead the q79 Fu–Yau heterotic branch. Conditional on an exact anomaly-free modular (0,2) worldsheet theory, GSO projection, factorization, and quantum-BV vertices, every fixed-genus, fixed-multiplicity amplitude has no local ultraviolet divergence. The holomorphic/HYM bundle, differential Bianchi representative, exact worldsheet packet, and all-genus or nonperturbative completion remain open.
title: Modal Triplet Theory: Perturbative Coherent-Sector Quantum Gravity and the Heterotic UV-Completion Boundary
